--- title: "Compressing an experiment" description: "One pass to a compressed dataset whose size does not depend on the rows; the same fit; shards that merge." order: 2 jupyter: python3 --- The universal model needs only one compressed row per stratum, an arm × cohort: the number of clusters $G_h$, the sum of the cluster summaries $\sum u_a$, and the sum of their outer products $\sum u_a u_a^\top$ (the [conditionally sufficient statistics post](https://jeffwong.github.io/posts/conditionally_sufficient_statistics/)). The cluster summary $u_a$ holds the blocks $(S^Y, S, S^T)$ of the cluster's rows. It is built during the pass and never stored. ::: {#fc4e7efd .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import polars as pl import ume from ume.testing import simulate_accounts df = simulate_accounts(20_000, seed=2026) exp = ume.annotate( df, cluster="account", instrument="Z", treatment="T", cohort="day", covariates=ume.covariates(x1=2.0, x2=2.0, kids=0, device=ume.categorical(reference="tv")), ).metrics(ume.mean("y", name="hours"), ume.ratio("N", "D", name="rebuffers_per_play")) cd = exp.compress() cd ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## A dictionary of sufficient statistics `cd` is a mapping from strata to compressed rows: ::: {#ec80e474 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} row = cd[ume.Stratum(Z=1, cohort=1)] row ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ``` ::: ::: Its first moments are the three blocks, summed over the stratum's clusters. $S_{00}$ counts rows, and the indicator columns of a categorical hold counts by level: ::: {#e8a37bd8 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} row.blocks()["S"] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## The same fit Fitting the compressed data gives the fit on the rows, to rounding error: ::: {#cbb3a72a .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} fit_rows, fit_compressed = exp.fit(), cd.fit() { "max |Δβ|": float(np.abs(fit_rows.beta - fit_compressed.beta).max()), "max relative |Δ cov|": float(np.abs(fit_rows.cov - fit_compressed.cov).max() / np.abs(fit_rows.cov).max()), } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` {'max |Δβ|': 1.6042722705833512e-13, 'max relative |Δ cov|': 6.091843483534045e-15} ``` ::: ::: ::: {#f4da689c .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} fit_compressed.effects() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## Shards Compressed rows add. Each shard can be compressed separately, on a different machine, and the results summed. A streaming `Compressor` needs the reference points and levels fixed before the pass, so we take them from the design that `compress` resolved: ::: {#930f03a9 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} design = cd.design shards = [ ume.Compressor(design).update(df.filter(pl.col("account") % 3 == k).sort("account")).finish() for k in range(3) ] merged = shards[0] + shards[1] + shards[2] float(np.abs(merged.fit().beta - fit_rows.beta).max()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` 1.5920598173124745e-13 ``` ::: ::: Rows of a cluster must not be split across shards. Shuffle by cluster before sharding; a merge that sees the same cluster twice is refused. ## Size The compressed dataset has the same size for 20,000 or 20 million accounts. It holds `len(cd)` strata with $1 + q + q^2$ numbers each, here: ::: {#1385cbd7 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} len(cd), cd.q, len(cd) * (1 + cd.q + cd.q**2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ``` (8, 78, 49304) ``` ::: :::
